findings.kind: reconnected historical native executable count boundary
findings.trace: for_constraints stores u32 color slots and accumulates per-color counts and prefix sums before it creates u32 original indexes; ConstraintCount independently narrows to u32 at uniform and dispatch. On a host and configuration capable of producing at least 2^32 incident records, u32 accumulation exceeds its range or narrows; earlier memory/allocation limits may prevent reaching this. The exact overflow outcome depends on compilation configuration. No array, graph, allocation, test or GPU operation was run.
findings.conditions: Requires an exceptionally large admitted host population and enough preceding resources; not evidence that normal workloads reach it.

findings.kind: conditionally newly assessed direct public API policy question; no unique count requested
findings.trace: ParticleInverseMass::PINNED plus PINNED yields EffectiveInverseMass(0). All necessary symbols are public exports. ConstraintViolation::multiplier_delta directly divides by its supplied response, while a separate response.distance_activity marks zero inactive; WGSL xpbd_solve separately returns invalid for denominator below 1e-12. If a caller directly invokes the CPU helper with violation 1, zero compliance, zero multiplier and the zero response without checking activity, the source formula is -1/0, mathematically negative infinity under ordinary IEEE-754 behavior. A subsequent zero-mass distance correction multiplies zero by that nonfinite value. The helpers do not themselves establish that this caller behavior is supported.
findings.conditions: A direct caller supplies an inactive response without the separate precondition; literal filename-only search across crates found the method call spelling only in test source, not a complete call graph and not proof external calls are absent. CPU and GPU are different surfaces; no equivalent-runtime or observed NaN claim.

findings.kind: new conditional source-level work-scaling candidate; alias and supported input policy open
findings.trace: For N variable-arity constraint records, each consisting of the same particle, each new record restarts at candidate color 0; for zero-based record k, candidates 0 through k-1 are occupied and rejected, then k is free. Thus the loop performs N(N-1)/2 occupied-candidate checks before assignments, excluding other work. A nonzero fixed-arity incidence can also admit repeated particle records; ConstraintSet::new computes the coloring synchronously before its upload/allocation. This is a mathematical count from source, not a timed or executed workload.
findings.conditions: Public input admits an unbounded high-degree graph unless external producer limits apply; actual ordinary mesh degrees, reachable sizes, platform timing and security impact remain unestablished. N may be far below the u32 overflow boundary.
historical_links: 774 ADDITIONAL-118 explicitly records greedy algorithm and allows empty and repeated particle addresses but does not decide the work-bound policy

findings.direction: Establish supported incidence/population limits and the acceptable coloring work bound; consider a bounded algorithm or structured admission while preserving valid empty records, conflict separation and deterministic order within each color.

nonfindings.text: ConstraintSet::new computes Coloring from the same incidence and immediately uploads that incidence using that permutation, so this construction path does not exhibit a mismatched-coloring input. Earlier broad membership and public reorder concerns remain separate.

Empty sets and variable-arity empty/repeated particle records are explicitly supported; zero compliance is the infinitely stiff limit. No universal nonempty, distinct-index, positive-compliance or finite-native-word policy is inferred.

ColorRange and Coloring retain private range/order data; identical underlying u32 or usize representations do not make particle index, original constraint index, reordered slot and schedule color interchangeable semantic owners. Compile-fail documentation was read only.
The 059 and 774 material read for coloring ended at line151; lines152–153 are a test module declaration independently read in the present task, not previously credited and not a test execution.
